OBSTACLES AND DIFFICULTIES
There is a possibility that it will be difﬁcult to ﬁgure out the placement and positioning when
installing the mirrors in the library. A potential obstacle the class might face with the mirrors is
stabilizing them. To address this problem, we will be using durable and sturdy materials and
making prototypes. The prototypes will help the design group ﬁgure out the visibility and
reﬂectiveness that the mirrors display. We need to ﬁgure out if the image that the librarian’s
going to see is going to be more clear or blurry.

Regarding materials, it might become difﬁcult to ﬁnd something that can both reﬂect in the
way we want it to, and ﬁt over the shell of the mirror correctly.
We plan on addressing these issues by testing multiple products what could provide the
reﬂective surface instead of just one.

We know that our end users will be satisﬁed with the ﬁnal design because of the amount of
testing we will be doing on the product. With thorough testing and experimentation, our team
will be able to ﬁnd the perfect angles, style, and positioning for the placement of the design in
the library.

Handle: The handle may not meet our design requirements if it is not attached to the body

our project. How we’ll avoid this: To avoid this problem we will measure our pieces of wood before
using them for our project. We will also purchase durable pieces of wood that we know will last for
a while.

Button: The button of the design may not meet our design requirements if it is not able to

move properly. If the button doesn’t move properly the balls will not be able to dispense. Examples
of the button malfunctioning would be it getting caught while sliding out of the way to allow the
ball to come out. How we’ll avoid this: We will avoid this problem by constructing our button
properly to ensure that it doesn’t get caught anywhere in our design.

Dispensing Mechanism: The dispensing mechanism may not meet our design requirements
if it does not shift in the proper direction to allow the balls to come out of the dispenser. How we’ll
avoid this: We will avoid this problem by constructing our dispensing mechanism with precision and
concentration to ensure that it doesn’t fail when it dispenses.

Wheels: The wheel of this design may not meet our design requirements if the wheels are
too small to handle the weight and capacity of our design. How we’ll avoid this: We will avoid this
problem by picking wheels that can sustain the weight of our project.

Element  F:   Consideration  of  Design  Viability 

 The  stakeholder’s  problem  was  including  special-need  students  and  helping  them  participate  in  large-size 
 physical  education  classes.  The  main  problem  was  that  these  students  had  limited  motor  skills  and  most  of  the 
 time  could  not  use  a  large  part  of  their  body.  As  a  result,  they  were  confined  to  walkers  and  wheelchairs  which 
 made  it  difficult  to  participate  in  typical  physical  activities.  Frisbees  help  create  an  entertaining  environment 
 and  can  be  easily  used  by  any  student.  The  proposed  solution  of  a  frisbee  launcher  that  was  developed  aimed  at 
 fulfilling  all  of  the  stakeholder's  needs  while  still  being  entertaining  for  the  students.  The  frisbee  launcher  was 
 designed  to  launch  a  frisbee  with  the  help  of  motors  rather  than  a  student’s  arm.  This  way,  a  game  of  frisbee 
 can  still  be  played  without  having  to  move  body  parts  around,  which  can  be  hard  or  impossible  for  these 
 students.  The  Frisbee  launcher  contains  a  subsystem  in  which  two  running  motors  are  connected  by  a  belt  to 
 create  a  pulley  system.  The  two  motors  have  a  flywheel  attached  to  them  which  causes  the  flywheels  to  spin  at 
 a  high  rate  of  speed.  As  a  result,  the  frisbee  that  passes  by  gets  a  thrust  of  power  and  will  shoot  out  similar  to  a 
 human-arm  throwing  one. 

 The  use  of  viable  materials  such  as  wood,  pulleys,  motors  and  flywheels  can  facilitate  the  development  of  a 
 realistic  prototype  for  the  user.  These  materials  are  easily  attainable  and  can  be  implemented  into  our  design  to 
 allow  the  frisbee  to  fly  at  the  desired  distance.  Similar  prototypes  have  been  built  using  wood  as  the  base  and  a 
 motor  system  to  make  the  flywheel  spin.  However,  in  these  prototypes,  the  motor  was  directly  underneath  the 
 flywheel,  while  the  proposed  design  to  the  user  requires  a  pulley  system,  which  uses  a  belt  to  connect  the 
 motor  to  each  axle  of  the  two  flywheels.  These  materials  were  also  easily  attainable  and  allowed  for  them  to  be 
 efficiently  used  into  the  development  of  the  prototype.

 with  limited  abilities  in  physical  activities.  However,  while  having  only  one  flywheel  would  be  sufficient  to 
 meet  the  user’s  needs,  the  proposed  prototype  consists  of  two  flywheels  which  can  shoot  the  frisbee  at  a  larger 
 distance.  In  addition,  instead  of  having  just  one  set  speed  to  shoot  the  frisbee  at,  speed  of  the  motor  can  be 
 adjusted  in  order  to  improve  the  feasibility  of  the  prototype.  Using  Arduino,  we  can  connect  the  motor  to  the 
 pins  and  manipulate  the  speed  by  decreasing  the  torque  of  the  motor.  The  solution  will  also  be  able  to  adjust  by 
 changing  the  angle  at  which  the  frisbee  can  be  launched.  By  changing  the 

 In  order  to  ensure  the  extra  aspects  of  the  prototype  were  compelling,  a  professor  at  George  Mason  University 
 reviewed  our  design.  While  the  professor  had  supported  our  ideas  for  a  double  flywheel  system,  he  also  had 
 concerns  about  the  added  weight  of  the  whole  mechanism.  In  order  to  add  the  second  flywheel,  there  would  be 
 many  other  parts  such  as  the  extra  material  to  mount  the  motor  and  the  pulleys.  However,  the  added  flywheel 
 would  allow  the  frisbee  to  shoot  farther  and  engage  the  students  even  more.  Furthermore,  the  extra  feature  of 
 changing  the  motor  speed  can  also  manipulate  the  distance  the  frisbee  will  fly.  This  allows  for  the  prototype  to 
 be  more  flexible  for  the  user  and  can  be  used  to  cater  the  needs  for  many  different  students.

The design is explicitly connected to the stakeholder's needs for special-needs students, emphasizing ease of use and engagement. The inclusion of expert input from a professor who reviewed the design and raised concerns about added weight demonstrates awareness of constraints and tradeoffs. The ability to adjust motor speed and launch angle further supports the design's flexibility and feasibility. However, the evidence lacks quantitative data or detailed testing results, and the risk analysis is limited to a single expert comment without deeper exploration of potential failure modes or mitigation strategies.
narrative_feedback:
Your design viability judgment is strong in that it clearly links the proposed frisbee launcher to the specific needs of special-needs students, emphasizing accessibility and engagement. You effectively support your claims by referencing the use of realistic, easily obtainable materials and citing similar existing prototypes, which adds credibility to your design's feasibility. The inclusion of expert feedback from a professor who reviewed your design is a valuable addition, showing you have considered potential constraints such as added weight and the tradeoffs involved in adding a second flywheel.

However, your evaluation could be strengthened by providing more detailed evidence, such as quantitative data or prototype testing results, to better demonstrate the design’s performance and reliability. Additionally, expanding your risk analysis to include other possible failure modes or challenges, along with strategies to address them, would improve the robustness of your viability judgment. To enhance your work, consider including specific measurements or test outcomes, elaborating on how you will mitigate identified risks, and clarifying how your design meets all major requirements in detail. This will provide a more comprehensive and convincing case for your design’s viability.

In order to begin construction of our portable sink, we must first identify the possible hazards
and threats of our construction process.

Items that could potentially cause issues and why they we can mitigate this:

- Over budget project: This is one of the most important issues to not have happen. For our
project we only have a total budget of about $200 for this project of outside materials that
we do not already have. In order to prevent this issue we are taking steps to calculate the
cost of each item we expect to buy in order to build the project and leaving a little bit of
space so that if there is an unexpected purchase needed we have room to add in the extra
cost. Further, while our calculated bill of materials exceeds $200 (+$16.57), we have
sourced the majority of our materials from in-school sources, offering them free of
charge(Note: the final bill of materials includes the estimated price the materials we
sourced for free would cost if we had to purchase these items). Furthermore, we are 100%
confident that the true cost of the project was below $200 as a majority of our materials
were in-house sourced, likely being worth more than the exceeded $16.57.

- Water being too slow: This problem can make or break the sink. If we run into this

problem our sink will be at a severe disadvantage to the teacher and students using the
regular sink as if you cannot perform the actions of washing your hands and brushing
your teeth than a sink in the context of a life skills class will not be useful. In order to
prevent this issue we have a valve that will control the speed of the water and allow more
to flow if needed. We also have the ability to widen the hole of the water storage if
needed as the storage container we are using has 2 holes with one being bigger than the
other to allow a faster flow. Further, we have also experimented with the inclusion of
multiple faucets, with different size holes, allowing for different amounts of water to
flow. It is safe to say that our prototype will be able to be adjusted by the stakeholder to
ensure the waterflow is not too slow. On the flip side, the sink's ability to use water from
two tanks at a time may allow for a water flow too strong for proper use of the sink. This
is also mitigated by the different faucets with different size holes, allowing the
stakeholder to control the flow outside of just the sink handles adjustability.

- Contamination and mold growth: Considering the fact that we are using an appliance that
provides water for brushing teeth and washing hands, it is very important that we use a
sink that can be easily cleaned, and has no space favorable to bacteria growth.
Conveniently, our sink’s entire surface will be constructed out of plastic. This will
facilitate easy cleaning via wipes, and no nooks or crannies which could allow bacteria
growth. Further when examining where the water makes contact with our sink, we’ve
determined there only being one potential area the bacterial growth may need to be
cleaned to avoid further deterioration of the sink. According to Johnathan T Blanton,
“stainless steel is the best material at resisting bacterial growth.” Further we acknowledge

that water makes contact with the stainless steel sink bowl, as well as the internal
compartment of the large plastic storage container. Moreover, the concern that the
bacterial growth in the sink is minimal, and should not draw bacterial growth due to the
frequency the sink will be used/flushed, as well as the materials ability to withsWith
proper instructions as to how to disinfect this internal compartment once a week should
ensure that our prototype mitigates the cleanliness concerns of the stakeholders, experts,
and possible investors.

Spillage: When working with water it is an usual occurrence for water to spill out and
make a mess. This is not ideal so it would be critical if we could prevent the spillage of
the water preventing messes in the classroom. In order to achieve this goal we are
utilizing the lid of the container to act as a lid on the sink that has edges to prevent
spillage. Another preventing measure is that we have more than enough room in the
bottom of our sink holding the gray water allowing enough space to hold the wastewater
and its contents without flow coming back up through the sink. Further our use of
water-proof grade water containers, allows us to ensure that this is not an issue.
Moreover, when looking at the sink faucet and handles, we have mitigated possible
leaking through the use of superglue to attach each piece. This will surprisingly mitigate
water leakage, as large amounts of the glue act as a sturdy solid barrier between the liquid
and external surfaces.
Stability: One issue that could happen is that the sink will tip due to the weight being
mainly put on one edge bottom container. This issue is rational and could happen if we
are not careful with the way we place our clean water storage. The way we mitigate this
is by proper placement of our clean water storage, we are expecting to put it on the top of
the storage bin’s lid but having it take up at least half of the lid on one side in order to
make sure the weight is distributed on each side. Another thing we can do to mitigate
unstableness is to add a counterweight or just weight into the container in order to make
the bottom more heavy than the top; however this could cause issues with overall weight
but we would just have to monitor the overall weight as we go to make sure that the sink
is still able to be picked up by an average person and the teacher more importantly.
Further, knowing we cannot work around the fact that the sink requires a waste storage
system as well as a water storage system, we understand the height and weight of the sink
can only be reduced and mitigated so much. Moreover, in the case it causes problems, we
have decided to recommend to the teachers to ensure the sink is in an area that may allow
it to rest next to the wall, to reduce the chance a student runs by and knocks it over.

- Lack of functionality or learning capabilities: One of the aspects of the projects that

makes this project engineering is the fact that we are making a portable sink and the fact
that it is being used in a classroom so a learning element should be included as well. One
issue we run into is the lack of having learning capabilities or the lack of functionality.
These two go hand in hand in making our sink so it is important for us to find a good
balance between the two. The most important of these 2 is the functionality of the sink.
However, adding in some learning capabilities will be excellent and will make our design
go much further in pleasing the customer. Our main concern in our design is
functionality, but we are deciding to add a learning capability if possible in the design.
Our ideas for adding in a learning feature is the addition of 3D printed sink handles that
model ones that are commonly used in the real world. This will allow students lacking
motor skills the ability to have experience and figure out how to operate different types of
handles that will appear as they traverse life. We also have decided to color code the
temperatures of the waters, to add a learning lesson in terms of which side gives what
temperature of water, and what the purpose is to have two sink handles.

Element F

The Nashville Zoo Veterinary Hospital serves to provide animal healthcare, providing essential

care to a diverse range of species. In emergency situations where heavy animals require medical

attention, the ability to lift and maintain them safely and securely is crucial to the hospital.

Recognizing this need, our project aims to design a heavy animal lift that meets the criteria

verified by our stakeholders. We have ensured that our project closely follows the established

range of criteria, including cost constraints, loading time, weight-bearing capacity, durability

under sustained use, ease of operation, balance, removability, and the mitigation of any potential

discomfort or harm to the animals involved.

Our design for the heavy animal lift centers around a sturdy framework engineered from bolted

electro-galvanized superstrut channels, reinforced with two-sided angle brackets to provide

stability and durability under heavy loads in multiple dimensions. This adaptable structure is

designed to work with existing equipment at the Nashville Zoo Veterinary Hospital,

incorporating a method for reusing ratchet straps to securely connect the lift to the provided

green tarp that is currently used for the Zoo’s field operations. We have taken numerous measure

to make the design as ergonomic and easily usable as possible by incorporating many adaptable

features and automated machine parts.

We chose to take the route of utilizing a galvanized steel such as Superstrut due to the extreme

durability and its improbability to bend under large loads. We initially settled on the material

known in the industrial world as Unistrut. Unistrut is a versatile umbrella of steel channels,

fittings, and accessories designed for constructing support structures in various applications. Its

properties include high strength, durability, and corrosion resistance. According to Unistrut

Buffalo Supports, “Unistrut is the original metal framing system featuring a unique weldless

connection. It eliminates welding and drilling, and is easily adjustable and reusable, for infinite

configurations. Over time, the brand has evolved from a simple connection concept to a

comprehensive engineered building and support system featuring a robust line of: Channels,

Fittings, Fasteners, Hangers, Pipe Clamps, and Accessories.” Since, Unistrut offers compatibility

with a wide range of accessories, it allows for customization and adaptability to different project

requirements. In other words, Unistrut is valued for its efficiency, reliability, and versatility in

many applications.

However, after consulting the brilliant engineer and research assistant Bill Rodriguez at

Vanderbilt University, we were introduced to a material called Superstrut, which is essentially

Unistrut that is designed for smaller scale applications. He suggested that this material would be

ideal for our application due to its cost-effectiveness and durability under loads similar to what

our design will experience.

According to Clayton S. Johnson, an engineer who has experience in utilizing both Unistrut and

Superstrut, Superstrut is a versatile metal framing system gaining popularity for its flexibility,

durability, and customization options across various applications like electrical, mechanical, and

industrial support. Its pros include versatility, ease of installation without welding or drilling, and

a high load capacity. However, it can be pricier in bulk than its rival, Unistrut, due to

higher-quality materials and a wider range of fittings. Additionally, its unique design may limit

compatibility with other strut systems, affecting integration with existing structures.

In the context of our design, however, we were not purchasing the Superstrut in bulk, nor did we

require it to work with Unistrut-proprietary parts, so we decided that Superstrut was best for our

project. We are extremely confident in the durability of the Superstrut not to bend under extreme

loads close to the 400 to 1100 pounds specified by the veterinary hospital, and thus believe the

framework of our design to be a viable solution to our task.

Another strength of our project was adapted from a suggestion by Bill Rodriguez to help keep

the lift balanced and create a point of attachment for the lift to the industrial coffing bottom hook

at the vet hospital. Mr. Rodriguez is experienced in working with heavy automobile engines and

often uses a bar engine leveler to remove engines from cars and keep them balanced as needed.

The engine leveler, as shown above, allows the user to adjust the fulcrum of the balance and

maintain the balance of a system regardless of the changing center of mass. The photo on the

right shows how, after slightly adjusting the fulcrum position, you can maintain the balance with

an uneven weight distribution. This capability is crucial for the design, as it completely

eradicates the past issue of maintaining the balance of the lift, which is essential for the

stakeholders at the hospital. Additionally, the load limit of the leveler is 1500 pounds, which

exceeds our maximum criteria of 1100 pounds. This system and its advantages help to make the

design in its entirety a viable solution to the given problem of the Nashville Zoo.

Our design group got to spend a day with experienced engineers, as well as the Nashville Zoo

Vet Hospital’s very own Dr. Stephen Wancea, and we were able to collect valuable input and

suggestions. NTC Award winning CCTE Director Jeremy Qualls told us that he likes our

framework and was impressed with the engine leveler that we utilized in our prototype. Some

additional suggestions by Mr. Qualls include a remote actuator for the engine leveler. Taking this

into consideration, we determined that we can actuate the fulcrum-adjuster with a handheld drill

(with the appropriate drill bit) in order to maximize efficiency and decrease the time required to

balance the animal, as this could be problematic for the doctors.

In considering the risks associated with each sub-part of our design, we have established a

primary issue brought to our attention by Mr. Wancea. First of all, due to the immense size of

many of the zoo’s animals, the straps are almost guaranteed to be in contact with the animals

throughout the process, meaning that the material used needs to be safe and comfortable when in

constant contact with the animal’s skin. Dr. Wancea at the Nashville Zoo explained how they

often use pool noodles or wire tubing to safeguard against any harm or irritation caused by straps

rubbing against the animals’ skin. We decided that taking the route of nylon straps would

eliminate the problems related to discomfort from the metal cables, a decision to which Dr.

Wancea was in agreement.

In summary, our design surpasses all of the given criteria and incorporates many suggestions by

both our stakeholders and experienced professionals in the engineering field. These same

professionals and stakeholders have assured us of our design’s viability and made sure to point

out areas that still need to be tested and improved. Our use of galvanized steel framework and

integration of a balancing mechanism show our careful consideration of the given criteria and the

usability of our design for the stakeholders.

Works Cited

Johnson, Clayton S. “Superstrut vs. Unistrut: Battle of the Struts.” Clayton Notes, 7 Apr. 2023,

claytonnotes.com/superstrut-vs-unistrut/.

“What Is Unistrut? - UNISTRUT Buffalo Supports.” Unistrut Buffalo Supports, Longest

Running Independent Supplier of Unistrut Metal Framing in the World!,

unistrutstore.com/what-is-unistrut. Accessed 13 May 2024. \

The student also addresses risks and constraints, such as animal comfort with strap materials and load limits, demonstrating thorough consideration of design viability.

The proposed design was carefully reviewed based on several relevant extra-

functional considerations; a judgment about design viability based on those
considerations — the capacity of the proposed solution to address the problem — is
clearly realistic and well supported with credible evidence.

Throughout many points in this journey, our group has gone through several specific

designs and iterations of designs before reaching our final design. The Andean Bear Zookeepers

challenged with the following criteria they wished to incorporate into our design.

A. Durability: Materials used should be sturdy and resilient to withstand the strength of the

bears. PVC (schedule 40 or schedule 80) and thick wood (4x4) are recommended.

B. Ease of Cleaning: Materials should be easy to clean to maintain hygiene standards.

Temporary Design: The puzzle should be temporary to allow for movement within the

habitat and dens.

C. Feeding-based Enrichment: The puzzle should primarily revolve around food to

incentivize the bears. However, other interactive elements like items to push can be

included.

D. Customization: The puzzle should be customizable to accommodate different sizes of

food items, with the largest portion being 2"x2" to 3".

E. Dimensions: The maximum size of the puzzle feeder should not exceed the dimensions of

a 31-gallon water drum (22 inches in diameter, 35 inches tall).

F. Mounting Requirement: Feeders for the habitat must be mounted securely to prevent

them from falling into the moat, pool, or hitting the glass. Inside dens, options for both

mounted and unmounted feeders are acceptable.

G. Attention Span Consideration: The puzzle should engage the bears for as long as

possible, ideally allowing them to return to it throughout the day. Attention spans vary

but can range from 5-10 minutes or until food is depleted.

For criteria A, we opted to use high-molecular-weight high-density polyethylene

(HMW-HDPE) than that of the recommended schedule 40 PVC. Although PVC has a higher

tensile strength than HMW-HDPE, the processing or cutting of PVC can release chloride gas,

compromising the safety of both bear consumption and student-use. HMW-HDPE is also more

resistant to fatigue cracking and failure due to its high concentration of polyethylene and used for

food-grade applications. See the resources page for more in-depth information.

For criteria B, the group decided to make disassembly an easy task. This allowed the final

design to be a simplification of the previous iterations and improved for optimal use. However,

some aspects of the final product deemed to be harder to disassemble in person than in theory.

This may be due to human error when manufacturing the puzzle. Additionally, some parts of the

barrel may not be washed due to the potential formation of pollutants or malfunction of the

puzzle. For example, the lazy susan may not be washed as the grease to allow the lazy susan will

wear off. Additionally, washing the grease off onto certain surfaces can damage the chemical

integrity of plastics. This can be solved by avoiding washing the lazy susan, which disassembly

can prove to be beneficial.

For criteria C, the use of a large container allows for room for zookeepers to add as much for

attracting the bear’s attention through gaps in the lid that allow for the scent of the food to pass

through, but not necessarily the food itself.

For criteria D, the customization of the puzzle can be varied as smaller objects can be

included inside of the puzzle to add combinations and variables to the puzzle. This can be altered

freely by the zookeepers as the large barrel can accomodate fairly mid-sized items.

For criteria E, the dimensions of the project is that of the listed size.

For criteria F, the outer parts of the puzzle consist of a clamp that seals the lid of the

barrel to the lip of the barrel. This clamp also has a pass-through hole to lock the clamp in place,

allowing the zookeepers to secure the lid close from the bear. This lock (sold separately) can be

used to attach a chain to the top the barrel, securing the barrel to the enclosure. The puzzle is not

required to have an attachment point, but having the option to do so can provide the randomness

factor and customization ability to the list.

For criteria G, the design incorporates randomness as a factor to allow the bear to face the

same object, but not the same objective. This was done by the addition of a human-removable

handle that will then provide the factor of randomness by allowing room for the bear to make

errors when trying to repeat the task of opening the lid the same fashion it has done before. This

ensures that the bear will never come across the same exact puzzle, but rather a variation.

The student also acknowledges potential risks and constraints, such as the difficulty in disassembling some parts and the grease on the lazy susan, and proposes practical mitigations. Your choice of HMW-HDPE over PVC is well justified with credible evidence regarding safety and material properties, showing a clear understanding of constraints and risks. The inclusion of multiple criteria and how your design addresses each one shows a comprehensive approach to viability. Finally, ensure all cited resources are fully integrated into your argument to maximize credibility.

Stakeholder Concerns and Connections
(A3, A4)
Primary stakeholders or stakeholder groups impacted by the need for electric scooter softball/baseball bags
include athletes, coaches, parents, and event organizers. Athletes are concerned about the practicality and

durability of the bags, as they need reliable equipment to transport their gear efficiently. Coaches are concerned
about the functionality and ease of use to ensure their team's equipment is organized and accessible. Parents
prioritize safety features and affordability when investing in sporting gear for their children. Event organizers
are concerned with the plan of transporting equipment to and from venues, seeking solutions that smooth the
process and minimize disruptions. Addressing the need for electric scooter softball/baseball bags is crucial as it
directly impacts the efficiency, safety, and overall experience of those involved in sports activities. Also,
neglecting this issue could lead to increased frustration, wasted time, and potential safety hazards, affecting not
only the primary stakeholders but also secondary stakeholders such as spectators, facility managers, and the
environment due to inefficient transportation methods and potential waste of resources.

Problem Importance
(A6)
In a world where efficiency, safety, and sustainability is crucial, the urgency for electric scooter
softball/baseball bags are undeniable. With participation in softball and baseball leagues surpassing 25.9
million individuals in the United States alone, the demand for gear transportation solutions is
evident (Sports & Fitness Industry Association). Traditional methods not only pose risks of strain injuries,
contributing to over 2.6 million annual emergency room visits among youth athletes (National Institutes of
Health) but also add to carbon emissions, as highlighted by studies in the International Journal of Sports
Science & Coaching. By embracing electric scooter bags now, we not only enhance player safety and well-
being but also align with global efforts to reduce environmental impact, making it important to address this
need quickly.

The problem is happening when you go to any sports field.

The problem happens due to the time it takes to walk to the field. It wastes valuable time.

Stakeholder Concerns and Connections
(A3, A4)
Primary stakeholders or stakeholder groups impacted by the need for electric scooter softball/baseball bags
include athletes, coaches, parents, and event organizers. Athletes are concerned about the practicality and

durability of the bags, as they need reliable equipment to transport their gear efficiently. Coaches are concerned
about the functionality and ease of use to ensure their team's equipment is organized and accessible. Parents
prioritize safety features and affordability when investing in sporting gear for their children. Event organizers
are concerned with the plan of transporting equipment to and from venues, seeking solutions that smooth the
process and minimize disruptions. Addressing the need for electric scooter softball/baseball bags is crucial as it
directly impacts the efficiency, safety, and overall experience of those involved in sports activities. Also,
neglecting this issue could lead to increased frustration, wasted time, and potential safety hazards, affecting not
only the primary stakeholders but also secondary stakeholders such as spectators, facility managers, and the
environment due to inefficient transportation methods and potential waste of resources.

Problem Importance
(A6)
In a world where efficiency, safety, and sustainability is crucial, the urgency for electric scooter
softball/baseball bags are undeniable. With participation in softball and baseball leagues surpassing 25.9
million individuals in the United States alone, the demand for gear transportation solutions is
evident (Sports & Fitness Industry Association). Traditional methods not only pose risks of strain injuries,
contributing to over 2.6 million annual emergency room visits among youth athletes (National Institutes of
Health) but also add to carbon emissions, as highlighted by studies in the International Journal of Sports
Science & Coaching. By embracing electric scooter bags now, we not only enhance player safety and well-
being but also align with global efforts to reduce environmental impact, making it important to address this
need quickly.

A difficulty that might occur would be trying to accommodate the size of the reservoir under the

structure. Since the current size of the structure can only accommodate a 30” by 60” box that would not

be enough for the hydroponics unit to work at its best. We may need to reconsider some things such as the

amount of material and resizing the structure to be able to fit a 3 gallon box under the structure. We plan

to address this problem by putting the water basin on the floor while the actual structure of the

hydroponics sits on the table. Which leads us to our second possible difficulty that might occur when

trying to build our prototype would be the water from the basin not pumping properly up to the structure

where the plants are planted. Since the design that we plan to build is on a CAD software and it has the

water basin located on the floor and the actual hydroponics structure is on the table that our stakeholder

wants it to be placed on. We are worried that the water pump would not be powerful enough to pump the

water from a low point to a high point. This of course would alter the price of the whole project whether it

is requiring more material to build, increasing the price/budget or requiring less material to build it,

decreasing the price/budget and it may also take extra time and thinking to find a better solution/better

place to put the water basin. Our plans to address this obstacle is possibly putting the water basin next to

the hydroponics and making the PVC pipes detachable/disassemble so it can accommodates our

stakeholders criteria of it being easy to put into storage. Another difficulty may be if our design can

accommodate the type of plants our stakeholder wants to grow. She wants to grow plants such as

strawberries, tomatoes, and bell peppers, which can grow up to between 1 foot to 10 feet tall. Our current

design had not taken into account the size and height of the plants being growing, which is an issue. We

plan to address this obstacle by installing removal trellises so that our stakeholder can use the trellises at

her own discretion. This allows our stakeholders to plant a wider variety of plants and does not just limit

them to plants that meet the height of the trellis or if they do not, plants that require trellis like small herbs

then they can remove the trellis. Generally speaking the removable trellises would satisfy our user’s needs

since it gives them more freedom to plant a variety of plants. Budget is a potential issue. Cedar planks are

the material we want to use for the wall portions of the structure, but the price of the planks may be over

our budget. With this in mind, we need to come up with alternative materials that fit our budget but still

have the same results we wanted from the cedar planks. Another obstacle is time. The plan is to have a

working design ready for the stakeholders by the end of the school year. This potentially may not happen.

To address this we could put in extra hours during the school day, working during a free period, rather

than just doing work during our class period. We could also take work home and get things done there and

bring it back ready to move ahead. As a solution to the budget issue. We have decided instead of using

Cedar Wood which is slightly over our budget, we would use an alternative wood called treated Pine

Wood for the structure of our hydroponics unit since it has similar resistance to decay, insects, and other

deteriorating factors as the cedar wood and it being within our budget it is an great alternative for Cedar

Wood. Additionally, the treated pine wood is lighter than cedar wood so it would accommodate the users'

needs. With these adjustments in mind. The user of the hydroponics would have an end result of a

waterproof hydroponic unit that looks aesthetically pleasing. Also they will know they will not have to

worry about the damages or problems that would occur with a non-waterproof material. Some obstacles

that we may encounter in this process are measurements being incorrect, features of the unit not being

correctly shown in the design, additions to design that change other aspects, and unexpected changes that

we may have to make to the design. With that in mind our team may have to alter the design because of

feedback from some of our stakeholders, which means the team would have to take their feedback and

implement it into the 3D model. Our team should be able to address these problems further by doing

group evaluations and collaborations to see how we as a team can solve the problem. The team have

confirmed that this tactic works with many group sessions having been conducted by both teams to

achieve the goal of an exceptional 3D design of the hydroponic unit. In order to ensure an up to standard

design the team will need to collaborate as a group on problems, which will address any type of obstacle

that comes our way.

spools. There will be one horizontal shelf compared to two vertical shelves. The pegs will be

extremely viable solution to the filament storage problem, specifically surrounding

the design requirements of easy organization, and ability to store 200 spools

printer filament, coming out at a total cost of $55.44, which is very reasonable for

an effective and realistic solution.

○ Mitigation: fully think through all the steps of building the final product, carefully
figure out the price for everything involved, and create an accurate budget.

● There could be difficulty in installing the shelf and pegs correctly.

○ Mitigation: completely measure the dimensions of the steel shelf beforehand and
